title: 1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship
text:
{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland | year = 1897 | image = | dates = | teams = | connacht = | munster = Limerick | leinster = Kilkenny | ulster = | matches = | poty = | team = Limerick | titles = 1st | captain = [[Denis Grimes]] | manager = | team2 = Kilkenny | captain2 = [[Jackie Walsh]] | manager2 = | totalgoals = | totalpoints = | topscorer = | previous = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1896|1896]] | next = [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1898|1898]] }} The '''All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1897''' was the 11th series of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], [[Ireland]]'s premier [[hurling]] [[single-elimination tournament|knock-out competition]]. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] won the championship, beating [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] 3–4 to 2–4 in the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |title=All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Roll of Honour |publisher=The GAA website |access-date=25 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110905085701/http://gaaweb.sitesuite.cn/page/roll_of_honour2.html |archive-date=5 September 2011 }} ==Format== '''All-Ireland Championship''' ''Semi-final:'' (1 match) This is a lone game which sees the winners of the Leinster [[championship]] play [[Galway GAA|Galway]] who receive a bye to this stage. One team is eliminated while the winning team advances to the final. ''Final:'' (1 match) The winners of the lone semi-final play the winners of the Munster championship. ==Provincial championships== ===[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=Quarter-final |team1=[[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] |score=2–3 – 1–4 |team2=[[Laois GAA|Laois]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium= [[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |score=2–6 – 2–6 |team2=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium= |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=Semi-final replay |team1=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |score=6–13 – 1–4 |team2=[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium= |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=16 October 1898
Final |team1=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |score=w/o – scr. |team2=[[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- ===[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]=== {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |score=2–5 – 2–3 |team2=[[Clare GAA|Clare]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Limerick]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=Semi-final |team1=[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |score=4–16 – 0–2 |team2=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Cork (city)|Cork]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- {{footballbox |date=Final |team1=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |score=4–9 – 1–6 |team2=[[Cork GAA|Cork]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Tipperary (town)|Tipperary]] |attendance= |referee= }} ---- ==All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship== ===All-Ireland semi-finals=== {{footballbox |date=30 October 1898
Semi-final |team1=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |score=3–4 – 0–4 |team2=[[Galway GAA|Galway]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance= |referee= }} ===All-Ireland Final=== Source:{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Matthew |date=2023-07-20 |title=Limerick's historic links with the GAA |url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/limericks-historic-links-with-the-gaa |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Limerick City and County Council}} {{footballbox |date=20 November 1898
Final |team1=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |score=3–4 – 2–4 |team2=[[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] |report= |goals1= |goals2= |stadium=[[Croke Park|Jones's Road]], [[Dublin]] |attendance=c.5,000 |referee= J. J. McCabe (Dublin) }} ---- ==Championship statistics== ===Miscellaneous=== * [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] win the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster championship]] for the first time. It was their fourth appearance in the final. * An All-Ireland semi-final is played for the first time since the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1887|1887 championship]]. That game is the first ever championship meeting of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. * The All-Ireland final is the first championship meeting of Kilkenny and Limerick. The win gives Limerick their very first championship. * Limerick become fifth team to win the All-Ireland hurling title. They become the fourth team to have won an All-Ireland title in both hurling and [[Gaelic football]]. ==Roll of Honour== *Cork – 4 (1894) *Tipperary – 3 (1896) *Limerick – 1 (1897) *Dublin – 1 (1889) *Kerry – 1 (1891) ==References== {{reflist}} ==Sources== * Corry, Eoghan, ''The GAA Book of Lists'' (Hodder Headline Ireland, 2005). * Donegan, Des, ''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' (DBA Publications Limited, 2005). {{Hurling All-Irelands}} [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championships|1897]] [[Category:1897 in hurling|All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] [[Category:1897 in Irish sport]]
